meta.titre: Table Setting and Meal Service: Laying a Cover, Service Styles and Manners
meta.sous_theme: Laying a cover, service styles, invitations and table manners

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A wedding reception in Bamenda is remembered for its food, but also for how the tables look and how politely the guests are served. The family sends printed invitations, lays the tables with clean cloths and decides whether the guests will be served at their seats or from a long buffet table. The GCE tests the same skills: which equipment is used to eat, how to lay a cover, which service style fits an occasion, and which manners are acceptable at the table.

items: Cutlery means knives, forks and spoons.
A menu is the list of dishes served at a meal.
Good hygiene applies to the table as well: plates and cutlery must be clean.

sections.titre: How to lay a cover and which equipment is used to eat
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Laying a cover
A **cover** is the space and the equipment for one person. Start with a clean, ironed cloth or table mats, then lay each cover:
- the plate in the centre, in line with the edge of the table;
- **forks on the left; knives and spoons on the right**, in the order of use from the **outside towards the plate**;
- the knife blade turned towards the plate;
- the glass on the right, above the knife; the side plate on the left, above the forks; the napkin on the plate or beside it;
- dessert spoon and fork either above the plate or brought with the dessert;
- salt, pepper and a centre piece such as flowers shared by the guests.
Lay only the equipment that the menu needs.

### Equipment used to eat

| Item | Use |
|---|---|
| Soup spoon | soup |
| Dinner knife and fork | main course |
| Fish knife and fork | fish course |
| Dessert spoon and fork | dessert |
| Teaspoon | tea, coffee, stirring |
| Butter knife | on the side plate, for bread and butter |
| Glass or goblet | water and drinks |
| Napkin | wiping the lips and fingers, protecting clothes |

### Good presentation
Use clean, polished equipment, matching plates, a fresh cloth and a tidy room. A neat table helps the meal to look appetising and makes guests feel welcome.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to name, describe or choose a way of serving a meal.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
- **Plate service**: food is dished onto plates in the kitchen and carried to each guest.
- **Family service**: dishes are placed on the table and the guests help themselves or the host serves.
- **Silver or waiter service**: a waiter serves the food from a dish onto the guest's plate at the table.
- **Buffet service**: food is displayed on a long table and guests serve themselves, so many people can be served quickly with few waiters.
- **Counter or cafeteria service**: guests queue at a counter and take a tray.
When describing a service, say who carries the food and who puts it on the plate.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked which occasions need a formal invitation, or for acceptable table manners.

sections.enonce_markdown: Describe how to lay one cover for a two-course meal of soup followed by a main dish with water to drink. (5 marks)

etapes.action: Analyse the command word and the marks.
etapes.justification: Describe means say how it is done, in a logical order. Five marks means about five clear points.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Write five numbered steps, from the base of the cover to the final touches.

etapes.action: List the items the menu needs.
etapes.justification: Soup needs a soup spoon, the main dish needs a knife and fork, water needs a glass, and bread would need a side plate.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Soup spoon, dinner knife, dinner fork, glass, side plate, napkin.

etapes.action: Fix the position of each item with the rules of laying.
etapes.justification: Forks go on the left, knives and spoons on the right, used from the outside inwards, so the first item used is the outermost.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Outside to inside on the right: soup spoon, then knife. On the left: fork.

etapes.action: Place the remaining items and finish.
etapes.justification: Glass is placed on the right above the knife, side plate on the left above the fork, and the napkin on the plate or beside it.

sections.conclusion_markdown: 1. Place the clean cloth or mat and put the dinner plate in the centre of the cover. 2. Lay the dinner fork on the left of the plate. 3. Lay the dinner knife on the right of the plate with the blade facing the plate, and the soup spoon outside it, because the soup is eaten first. 4. Put the glass on the right above the knife and the side plate on the left above the fork. 5. Fold the napkin and place it on the plate or on the left, and check that every piece is clean and straight.

items.erreur_markdown: Laying the forks on the right and the knives on the left.
items.pourquoi_faux: The standard rule is forks on the left, knives and spoons on the right.
items.correction_markdown: Left: forks. Right: knife, then spoon. Use them from the outside inwards.

items.erreur_markdown: Turning the knife blade away from the plate.
items.pourquoi_faux: The blade is turned towards the plate; a blade facing outwards is untidy and can hurt.
items.correction_markdown: Always lay the cutting edge of the knife towards the plate.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing the manners as: be polite, behave well, respect people, be good.
items.pourquoi_faux: These are vague. The examiner wants specific table habits and gives no mark for general words.
items.correction_markdown: Name actions: do not talk with food in the mouth, use the napkin, wait for everybody, ask for dishes to be passed.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that in a buffet the waiter brings each course to the guest at the table.
items.pourquoi_faux: In a buffet the guests walk to the table and serve themselves. Bringing food to the guest describes waiter or plate service.
items.correction_markdown: Buffet: self-service from a long table. Waiter service: food brought and served at the table.

items.enonce_markdown: Complete: (a) Forks are laid on the ______ of the plate. (b) Knives and spoons are laid on the ______. (c) Cutlery is used from the ______ inwards. (d) The glass is placed above the ______. (e) Which item is used to eat soup?
items.solution_markdown: (a) **left**; (b) **right**; (c) **outside**; (d) **knife** (on the right); (e) **the soup spoon**. (Award a mark for each.)

items.enonce_markdown: A hostess lays the table for 12 guests for a three-course dinner. Each guest needs a soup spoon, a dinner knife, a dinner fork, a dessert spoon and a dessert fork, and four plates and bowls: a dinner plate, a soup bowl, a side plate and a dessert plate. (a) How many pieces of cutlery are needed? (b) How many plates and bowls? (c) State two rules for placing the cutlery.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Cutlery per guest: 5 pieces. $12 \times 5 = 60$, so **60 pieces of cutlery**. (b) Plates and bowls per guest: 4. $12 \times 4 = 48$, so **48 plates and bowls**. (c) Any two of: forks on the left and knives and spoons on the right; cutlery laid in the order of use from the outside inwards; knife blades turned towards the plate.

items.enonce_markdown: Mr Tabe organises a wedding reception for about 150 guests. (a) Name the type of invitation he should send and give four details it must contain. (b) Suggest a suitable style of service and give two reasons. (c) State two acceptable table manners the guests should show.
items.solution_markdown: (a) A **formal (written or printed) invitation**, sent in advance. Details: the names of the hosts and the guest, the occasion, the date, the time, the place, the dress code, and RSVP (a line for the reply); any four. (b) **Buffet service** (plate service with enough waiters is also acceptable if reasons are given). Reasons: many guests can be served quickly; fewer waiters are needed; guests choose how much they eat. (c) Any two of: wait to be served or for the host to begin; keep the mouth closed when chewing; do not talk with food in the mouth; use the napkin; ask for dishes to be passed.

items_markdown: A cover is the space and equipment for one person: plate in the centre, forks on the left, knives and spoons on the right, glass above the knife, side plate on the left.
Cutlery is used from the outside inwards, and the knife blade faces the plate.
Know the styles of service: plate, family, waiter or silver, buffet and counter, and who carries the food in each.
Formal invitations are used for weddings, graduations, official dinners, receptions and banquets; informal ones for family and friends.
Give table manners as specific actions, and write exactly the number of points asked.
